newsitem.title: USA: Fed policy won't greatly cut inflation - economists.
newsitem.headline: Fed policy won't greatly cut inflation - economists.

text.p: The Shadow Open Market Committee urged the Federal Reserve on Monday to focus its efforts on achieving stable prices, and argued that the central bank's current policy will not greatly reduce inflation.
The SOMC, a group of academic and business economists, recommended that "the Federal Reserve reduce the growth rates of the monetary base and other monetary aggregates to achieve zero inflation.
The SOMC said current inflation of two to three percent was too high and needed to be reduced.
"We believe that current (Fed) policy, if maintained, will not substantially reduce inflation below current levels," the group said.
The SOMC argued that increases in real wages do not cause inflation. In the past, wage increases were associated with rising inflation because inflationary Fed policy generated extra demand.
"Proper Fed policies break that link," the SOMC said.
